title: Seed Sensitivity of Emergent Misalignment: A Reproducibility Audit

original_idea.body:
# Seed Sensitivity of Emergent Misalignment: A Reproducibility Audit

**Problem:** The 12-model study reported emergent misalignment as 'consistent across seeds' in only 2/12 models, implying high run-to-run variance. The community lacks a clear picture of how seed-fragile the effect is, which undermines both attack and defense claims.

**Direction:** Fix one susceptible small open model and recipe, then run the insecure-code fine-tune across many random seeds (e.g., 10-20) and characterize the distribution of broad-misalignment rates. Twist: replicate a single condition many times to quantify variance rather than report a point estimate.

**Why it matters:** Reproducibility variance directly affects how seriously to treat the threat and how to design defenses/evals. A rigorous variance characterization is exactly the unglamorous, lab-deprioritized work that strengthens the whole subfield's evidentiary base.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2506.11613 found only 2/12 open models show emergent misalignment 'consistent across seeds', signaling large variance. Betley et al. (arXiv:2502.17424) supply recipe and eval. Variance characterization needs only repeated cheap LoRA runs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (variance grounds the evidence base) but indirect to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Repeat one LoRA finetune across many seeds + eval; guided and accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused variance characterization of a single condition; cohesive (many cheap runs).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Unglamorous, lab-deprioritized reproducibility work; open setup; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Many small LoRA runs but each cheap; feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Seed fragility noted; a dedicated variance audit may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Variance noted; dedicated audit may be open.
